sections.overview: The Wreathed Hornbill is a large forest hornbill of South and South-East Asia.
sections.identification: The male has a pale yellow gular pouch crossed by a dark band; the female’s head and throat are darker.
sections.habitat: It depends mainly on extensive evergreen forest, from lowlands into foothills, and may also use mangroves.
sections.diet: Fruit, especially figs, forms much of its diet, supplemented by animal prey such as insects and small vertebrates.
sections.behavior: It forages in the canopy and can travel in noisy groups between feeding sites.
sections.reproduction: The female seals herself inside a tree cavity during nesting and depends on the male to bring food.
sections.ecology: A Thai study of hornbill-dispersed fruits included this species among the fruit consumers.
sections.conservation: BirdLife assesses it as Vulnerable, citing forest loss and hunting pressure.

sources.title: Characteristics of hornbill-dispersed fruits in Thailand — Bird Conservation International
